title: Construct slab models and compute low-coverage adsorption energies
action: For each of the eight target materials (SnTiO₃, CaTaO₂N, MgTaO₂N, LaTiO₂N, SrTaO₂N, BaTaO₂N, CaGeO₃, SrGeO₃), build BO₂‑terminated (100) perovskite slabs with a 2×2×4 supercell and 10 Å of vacuum. Perform DFT relaxation using Quantum Espresso with the RPBE functional and appropriate pseudopotentials to compute total energies of the clean slab and with OH*, O*, OOH*, and H* adsorbates at a coverage of θ=0.25 ML.
description: Intermediate DFT calculations that produce adsorption energies. No scored output directly from this step; the derived overpotentials are scored in the next step.

title: Calculate low-coverage theoretical overpotentials
action: From the adsorption energies obtained in the previous step, apply the computational hydrogen electrode (CHE) model including harmonic free-energy corrections to derive the low‑coverage theoretical OER and HER overpotentials for all eight materials. Write the results to a CSV file.
description: Low‑coverage overpotentials for the eight perovskite materials.
output_schema: CSV with columns: material (string), η_HER_low (float), η_OER_low (float); one row per material.

title: Compute surface oxygen vacancy formation energies
action: For each of the eight materials, compute the total energy of the slab with a surface oxygen vacancy at θ=0.25 ML and calculate the vacancy formation energy ΔE_vac relative to H₂O at 0 V vs. RHE. Write the results to a CSV file.
description: Surface oxygen vacancy formation energies for the eight materials.
output_schema: CSV with columns: material (string), ΔE_vac (float); one row per material, in eV.

title: Compute adsorption energies at high O* coverage (θ_O = 0.75 ML)
action: For the six non‑germanate materials (SnTiO₃, CaTaO₂N, MgTaO₂N, LaTiO₂N, SrTaO₂N, BaTaO₂N), directly set the background O* coverage to θ_O = 0.75 ML (the most stable coverage identified in the paper) and run DFT calculations to obtain total energies of the slab with this background and with additional OOH* and OH* adsorbates. No surface phase diagram construction is required.
description: Intermediate DFT calculations for the high‑coverage regime, directly using the known stable coverage. No separate stability analysis is performed.

title: Calculate high-coverage OER overpotential
action: Using the high‑coverage adsorption energies from the previous step (background θ_O = 0.75 ML), apply the computational hydrogen electrode (CHE) model with harmonic free-energy corrections to compute the OER overpotential at this high coverage for the six materials. Write the results to a CSV file.
description: High‑coverage OER overpotentials for the six non‑germanate materials.
output_schema: CSV with columns: material (string), η_OER_high (float); one row per material, in V.

title: Retrieve bandgap data from Castelli et al.
action: Obtain the direct and indirect bandgap values for the eight materials from the published data of Castelli et al. (2012) or the Computational Materials Repository. Format the data as a CSV file.
description: Direct and indirect bandgaps from the literature.
output_schema: CSV with columns: material (string), direct_bandgap (float), indirect_bandgap (float); one row per material, in eV.

title: Evaluate total water splitting feasibility
action: Combine the band‑edge positions (derived from bandgaps) with the computed overpotentials (low and high coverage) and vacancy formation energies. Apply a 0.5 eV photovoltage margin and determine, for each material, whether it can simultaneously drive HER and OER at pH 7 without degrading. The checker will verify this conclusion programmatically from the submitted data; no separate scored artifact is required.
description: Logical evaluation step; the conclusion is verified by the hidden checker using the submitted CSVs.
